Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. We're excited to get the ClearVista pilot started. Before we move to the technical onboarding, our legal and security teams asked for a short write-up on how Redwood will treat ClearVista data when we use the hosted inference API. Specifically we need confirmation and operational details for: 

- A firm "no-training" / "no model improvement" commitment for our tenant (no use of prompts/responses to update or fine-tune any internal/external models).
- Clarification on prompt/response ownership and whether generated content is licensed back to us.
- Data routing/residency options (we need onshore processing for EHR-derived content).
- Complete list of subprocessors (and whether any subprocessors have access to raw prompts).
- Evidence we can provide to auditors (SOC2 report pointer, export logs, attestation language).

I've attached a short list of questions our procurement team compiled (ClearVista_DPA_Questions.docx). Can you confirm what we should expect from Redwood (high‑level is fine) and whether we should sign the standard DPA or expect redlines?

Two asks if possible: a brief technical note for my engineers on how the no-training opt-out is implemented, and a small mutual action plan (MAP) with approximate timings for the pilot.

Best,
Elena

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then a proposed MAP below.

High level:
- No-training: We can commit to a tenant-level "no model improvement" setting for your pilot. That means prompts and responses are excluded from any internal model training pipelines and will not be used to update our models. We implement this as a routing flag at request time that keeps traffic on a non-learning inference fleet.
- Ownership: By default our terms grant customers a broad right to use generated outputs; we do not assert ownership over customer prompts or generated responses. We will add an explicit clause in the pilot DPA to reflect that.
- Residency: Hosted can be pinned to a US region; for strict onshore needs we offer Dedicated pools or a Private deployment.
- Subprocessors: We maintain an up-to-date subprocessors list; I'll attach the current CSV.
- Evidence: We can provide SOC2 report access, request-level logs for the pilot, and an operational attestation describing the no-training flow.

Proposed MAP (quick):
1) Legal: exchange DPA redlines (this week) — Marissa will lead.
2) Security: technical note + subprocessors sheet (tomorrow) — David will lead.
3) Ops: environment and routing tests (within 7 business days after step 2).
4) Kickoff: pilot start after sign-off.

I attached a short factsheet that may help your security team (redwood-no-train-factsheet.pdf). David, please add the technical specifics to this thread (KV cache behavior, model variant routing, logs, KMS). Marissa, I'll defer to you on DPA redlines and the attestation language.

Happy to jump on a call if you prefer.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Elena / team —

Technical detail below (concise):

1) No-training toggle (implementation)- We attach a tenant-level header (x-rw-no-train: true) on requests. The routing layer recognizes the flag and routes traffic to an inference pool that is explicitly excluded from any model update pipelines. That pool uses a pinned model binary (variant-id: rw-infer-stable-nolearn-v1) and has no write path into our training data lake.

2) Caching & KV state- Short-term KV caching is used to improve latency for streaming sessions but KV entries for no-train tenants are ephemeral and are never flushed into any persistent training store. We retain ephemeral runtime caches only for the duration of the session; no offload to analytics or training queues.

3) Logs & exportability- Request/response logs for the pilot can be exported via SFTP or pulled through an API with filters (time range, request id). We can redact or omit prompts from logs on request, but for auditability we can provide signed, time-stamped export bundles.

4) Subprocessors & access- Most subprocessors are cloud infra and monitoring vendors. Subprocessor list: https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors/subprocessors_20270401.csv (link) — none of the listed subprocessors have access to persistent prompt storage for no-train tenants. Access to raw prompts is limited to systems in the non-learning fleet and to operators under strict escalation and logging.

5) KMS & residency- For onshore-only requirements we can pin a Dedicated pool with customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) or deploy Private. For hosted with US-only routing we ensure VM placement and egress controls within the requested region.

If helpful I can prepare a short one‑page technical attestation that your auditors can accept.

-David
